author: Stan Boney
title: Mahoning EMA says county won't get money from state for storm cleanup - NewsBreak
text:
By Stan Boney ,
1 hours ago
BOARDMAN, Ohio (WKBN) — Gertrude Avenue in Boardman on Wednesday looked like many other township streets — lined with branches for pick-up after Sunday’s storm.
The aftermath dominated the discussion at Wednesday’s Boardman Township Trustees meeting, where they learned not to expect any money from the state or federal governments.
Zach Williams of the Mahoning County Emergency Management Agency told Boardman Trustees not to expect any money from the state or federal governments to help with cleaning up after Sunday’s storm.
The federal government requires that at least 24 houses sustain 40% damage and that they are uninsured.
“We don’t have that much damage to meet those directives that they need,” Williams said. “Right now we’re not really seeing those stats meeting their standards.”
Williams said most of the county’s power should be restored Wednesday by 11 p.m., except for the Fairway Drive area of Canfield, which could be out until the weekend.
“We are down under 800 residents who are left in the county that is without power. So we’re doing pretty good, where we started at over 23,000,” Williams said.
Assistant Fire Chief Bill Glaser said they received 400 calls for service, but one other statistic surprised him even more.
“It still amazes me that there were no injuries treated by us or Lane ambulance from the storm. And we had trees down on cars, we had people stuck in high water,” Glaser said.
Steve Yacovone joined his fellow trustees in complimenting how the employees of Boardman Township handled the aftermath.
“It doesn’t look like a tornado blew through here, and it’s been three days,” Yacovone said. “To see how everyone stepped up in a time of crisis, it was truly amazing.”
Williams, however, wanted to remind everyone that the cleanup is nowhere close to being over.
“It’s going to take weeks, and possibly even a month or two, in order to get all of that cleaned up,” Williams said.
